answers.answer: Factory deck is placed on the Factory territory. Encounter tokens are placed on designated territories. Structure bonus setup is not described; only that final coins include structure bonus tile coins (which vary). Who starts is not stated.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place encounter tokens on designated territories. Place the Factory card deck on the Factory territory.” Final Scoring: “Plus structure bonus tile coins (varies).”

answers.answer: The character starts on the faction's home base and one worker on each adjacent territory. Power and popularity markers start at positions that vary by Faction mat. Starting combat cards, coins, and objective cards are received as indicated, but the summary does not specify their amounts or clearly identify which mat supplies each. Other map and mat starting pieces are not specified.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Place the character on the faction's home base and one worker on each adjacent territory. Set combat power and popularity markers at starting positions (varies by Faction mat). Receive starting combat cards, coins, and objective cards as indicated.”

answers.answer: Yes, you may take one action, both, or neither, but must move your action token. You cannot repeat the same section as your previous turn, except Rusviet may repeat the same action section on consecutive turns. The summary says to perform the top-row action before the optional bottom-row action, but does not explicitly say whether taking the bottom action first is prohibited. Whether top-row gains can be spent on the bottom action is not stated. Bottom-row actions are described as paying their cost and gaining their benefit; exact costs are shown in the action descriptions, with Produce's cost variable.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “You may take one action, both, or neither, but you must move your token.” Turn step: “cannot repeat the same section as your previous turn.” Rusviet exception: “can repeat the same action section on consecutive turns.”

answers.answer: The summary says resources on a territory belong to whoever controls that territory, but does not explain who controls a structure territory occupied by an enemy worker or who can use its structure. For action spending elsewhere, the summary only states that Trade resources are gained on territories you control with workers; it does not state the general locations from which resources may be spent.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: “Resources on a territory belong to whoever controls that territory.” Trade: “Gain 2 resources of your choice on territories you control with workers.”

answers.answer: On a normal Move, up to two units may each move one territory; the summary does not say a unit can move twice. Mechs can carry workers, and workers carry resources. Whether a worker transported by a mech may then move separately is not stated.
answers.evidence: Move: “Move up to 2 units (character, worker, or mech) one territory each.” “Mechs can carry workers. Workers carry resources.”

answers.answer: A unit entering a territory with opponent workers forces them to retreat, with a loss of 1 popularity per retreating worker. The summary does not specify whether Speed-enabled movement changes this, whether the rule applies at zero popularity, or whether the mech's workers may enter the territory alone.
answers.evidence: Move: “Moving into a territory with opponent workers forces them to retreat (lose 1 popularity per retreating worker).”

answers.answer: Combat occurs when your character or mechs share a territory with an opponent's character or mechs after movement. The summary does not specify who chooses the order of multiple combats. It says workers cannot initiate combat and only characters and mechs fight, but does not explain whether workers can enter or leave territory controlled by an enemy character or mech alone.
answers.evidence: Combat: “When your character/mechs share a territory with opponent character/mechs after movement.” Special Rules: “Workers cannot initiate combat. Only characters and mechs fight.”

answers.answer: Bolster costs $1 and gives either 2 Power or 1 Combat Card. Trade costs $1 and gives either 2 resources of your choice on territories you control with workers or 1 Popularity. The summary does not say what happens if all workers are home or if the combat deck is exhausted.
answers.evidence: Bolster: “(pay $1): Gain 2 Power on the Power Track, OR draw 1 Combat Card.” Trade: “(pay $1): Gain 2 resources of your choice on territories you control with workers, OR gain 1 Popularity.”

answers.answer: Produce has a variable cost. Choose up to 2 territories you control with workers; each worker on those territories produces 1 resource matching the terrain (Forest Wood, Mountain Metal, Tundra Oil, Farm Food, Village Worker). The summary does not say how the cost is paid, where new workers come from, whether benefits may be declined, or whether new workers change the cost already paid.
answers.evidence: Produce: “(pay variable cost): Choose up to 2 territories you control with workers. Each worker on those territories produces 1 resource matching the terrain.”

answers.answer: Upgrade costs Oil: move a technology cube from a green top-row box to a red bottom-row box to improve action efficiency. Deploy costs Metal: place a mech on a territory with workers and unlock a faction-specific mech ability for your character and all mechs. Placement restrictions beyond “on a territory with workers” and whether a completed bottom action can still be paid are not stated.
answers.evidence: Upgrade: “(pay Oil): Move a technology cube from a green box (top-row) to a red box (bottom-row).” Deploy: “(pay Metal): Place a mech on a territory with workers.”

answers.answer: Build costs Wood and places a structure on a territory with workers, with at most one structure per territory. The summary does not say whether structures can move or be destroyed. A Mill counts as an extra territory for Produce; a Mine acts as a personal tunnel adjacent to all other tunnels. How either works when its territory is occupied by enemies is not stated.
answers.evidence: Build: “Place a structure on a territory with workers (max 1 structure per territory).” Structure effects: “Mill: Counts as extra territory for Produce. Mine: Acts as a personal tunnel (adjacent to all other tunnels).”

answers.answer: Enlist costs Food and places a recruit token, granting one one-time bonus: 2 Power, 2 Coins, 2 Popularity, or 2 Combat Cards. Its ongoing bonus is the specified bonus whenever you or adjacent players take that bottom-row action. The summary does not specify where the token is placed, which action sets its ongoing bonus, or how simultaneous/two-player bonuses resolve.
answers.evidence: Enlist: “Place a recruit token, gaining a one-time bonus (2 Power, 2 Coins, 2 Popularity, or 2 Combat Cards). Ongoing bonus: Gain the specified bonus whenever you OR adjacent players take that bottom-row action.”

answers.answer: Each combatant secretly selects power from 0 to their current power and may add up to 1 combat card per unit involved; reveal is simultaneous. Highest total wins and the attacker wins ties. The summary does not explain combat abilities or specify further payment/resolution rules for the dial and cards.
answers.evidence: Combat: “Both players secretly select power on their dial (0 to current power). Each player may add up to 1 combat card per unit involved. Reveal simultaneously. Highest total wins (attacker wins ties).”

answers.answer: The winner stays on the territory, keeps resources, and places a combat star. The loser retreats all units to their home base and gains 1 combat card if they committed any power. Popularity changes beyond the separate rule that retreating workers cost 1 popularity per worker are not described.
answers.evidence: Combat: “Winner: Stays on territory, keeps resources, places combat star. Loser: Retreats all units to home base, gains 1 combat card if they committed any power.”

answers.answer: An encounter is triggered when the character moves onto an encounter token, after all movement and combat. Draw a card with three options and choose one; options can grant resources, popularity, power, etc. The summary does not state what happens if the character loses a contested entry, where encounter gains are placed, or whether normal action costs or bonuses apply.
answers.evidence: Move: “Moving character onto an encounter token triggers an encounter after all movement/combat.” Special Rules: “draw a card with three options. Choose one (gain resources, popularity, power, etc.).”

answers.answer: The first character to reach the Factory gains a Factory card, which provides a fifth action section on that player's mat. The summary does not say whether later visitors may take one or change cards, or how Factory actions and Speed movement differ from mat actions.
answers.evidence: Factory: “The first character to reach the Factory gains a Factory card providing a 5th action section on their Player mat.”

answers.answer: A completed Objective Card is listed as an achievement for placing a star. The summary does not state when it may be revealed, its requirements, what is discarded, or what changes for Saxony.
answers.evidence: Star Placement: “Reveal a completed Objective Card.”

answers.answer: Listed star achievements are completing all 6 Upgrades, deploying all 4 Mechs, building all 4 Structures, enlisting all 4 Recruits, placing all 8 Workers, revealing a completed Objective Card, winning combat (maximum 2 stars except Saxony unlimited), reaching 18 Popularity, and reaching 16 Power. Whether stars can be lost or another player can block a goal is not stated. The game ends immediately when any player places their 6th star.
answers.evidence: Star Placement lists the achievements and Saxony exception. Game End Trigger: “The game ends immediately when any player places their 6th star on the Triumph Track.”

answers.answer: The summary says bottom-row actions are performed by paying the cost and gaining the benefit, and the game ends immediately when a player places their sixth star. It does not specify what is collected before ending, how pending battles resolve, or whether a neighbor's recruit star is earned.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: “Bottom-Row Action (optional): Perform the bottom-row action of that section (pay cost, gain benefit).” Game End Trigger: “The game ends immediately when any player places their 6th star.”

answers.answer: At 10 Popularity the player is in Tier 2 (7–12). The table awards $4 per star, $3 per controlled territory, and $2 per pair of resources. Five stars add $20; four normal territories plus Factory (five territories) add $15. Thirteen resources provide six complete pairs, adding $12, for $47 total from these categories; treatment of an unpaired resource is not specified. Structure bonus tile coins are added, but eligibility is not specified. The stated winner is the player with the most total coins; further victory tiebreakers are not given.
answers.evidence: Final Scoring: “7-12 = Tier 2”; table: “Per Star placed $4,” “Per Territory controlled $3,” “Per 2 Resources controlled $2.” “Plus structure bonus tile coins (varies). Player with the most total coins wins.”
